title: Trade-in estimate in phone checkout
overview: Trade-in estimate in phone checkout for Nimbus Wireless customers on app or web. Headline ask: Customers should be able to enter their current device model and condition during phone checkout and see an estimated trade-in value. This spec captures 6 functional and 3 non-functional requirements, 6 tracking events, the rollout and test plan, and the open questions the request leaves unanswered (section 15).
problem_statement: Customers who upgrade their phone often abandon checkout at the trade-in step because they don't know what their current device is worth until after they ship it. Trade-in value is one of the top questions in upgrade calls to care. We want to give customers an instant estimate before they commit.
goals: Increase checkout completion for upgrade orders
Reduce trade-in related calls to care
non_goals: Trade-in for tablets and wearables (phones only for now)

functional_requirements.description: Customers should be able to enter their current device model and condition during phone checkout and see an estimated trade-in value.
The estimate must be applied as a credit preview in the order summary.
Customers must be able to skip the trade-in step and continue checkout.
The estimate must come from the existing Trade-In Pricing Service.
Show a disclaimer that the final value is confirmed after device inspection.
Track the funnel from trade-in step viewed to estimate shown to order placed.

non_functional_requirements.description: The estimate should load fast [measurable target for 'fast' TBD: OQ-3].
All new UI on app or web meets WCAG 2.1 AA (screen-reader labels, 4.5:1 contrast, full keyboard/switch access).
Tracking events contain zero PII: no names, phone numbers, free-text message content or full account/card numbers.
The flow should be easy to use [measurable target for 'easy' TBD: OQ-3].

edge_cases.scenario: Trade-In Pricing Service times out or returns an error
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Show a non-blocking error state, let the customer continue, and fire `trade_in_estimate_failed` with error_code.

edge_cases.scenario: Customer skips the step, then navigates back to it
edge_cases.expected_behavior: The step is shown again with nothing pre-applied; no duplicate credit is created.

edge_cases.scenario: Customer in a group whose eligibility is unresolved (OQ-1: Are Nimbus Prepaid customers eligible?)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Behaviour follows the answer to OQ-1; until it is resolved the feature stays hidden for that group.

edge_cases.scenario: Customer starts on app and finishes on web (or vice versa)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Same content on both; events keep identical names and differ only in `platform`.

edge_cases.scenario: Analytics is blocked or consent is declined
edge_cases.expected_behavior: The feature works normally; no events are sent and no errors are shown.

risks.description: Event names drift between app and web, breaking the cross-platform funnel
risks.mitigation: Treat section 7 as the single source; lint against the event dictionary in CI.

risks.description: Trade-In Pricing Service latency or outage degrades the experience
risks.mitigation: Timeouts with graceful fallback; alert on the failed-event rate.

risks.description: 1 blocking open question(s) delay build start
risks.mitigation: Review open questions with owners before sprint planning.

risks.description: Experiment is under-powered for the expected effect
risks.mitigation: Size the test once the MDE is agreed.

assumptions.statement: Accessibility follows the company default of WCAG 2.1 AA.
Analytics events must not carry PII; this is standard instrumentation policy.
API contracts below are placeholders until the owning team confirms them.
Rollout stages follow the standard flag-based ramp.

open_questions.question: Are Nimbus Prepaid customers eligible?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The request explicitly leaves this open; it changes scope or eligibility logic.

open_questions.question: Should we A/B test the placement of the trade-in step?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The request explicitly leaves this open; it changes scope or eligibility logic.

open_questions.question: What measurable target defines 'fast', 'easy' in: "The estimate should load fast and the flow should be easy to use"?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Without a threshold the requirement cannot be tested or accepted.

open_questions.question: What is the target and timeframe for: "Increase checkout completion for upgrade orders"?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Success metrics need a target to size the rollout and judge the launch.

open_questions.question: What is the target and timeframe for: "Reduce trade-in related calls to care"?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Success metrics need a target to size the rollout and judge the launch.

open_questions.question: Which care-contact data source and reason codes identify the calls in: "Reduce trade-in related calls to care"?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The metric cannot be computed from app/web events alone.

open_questions.question: What are the primary metric, minimum detectable effect and planned duration of the experiment?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Needed to size the test and decide when to stop it.

open_questions.question: Is `trade_in_estimate_viewed` the same user action as existing `trade_in_quote_viewed`? If so, reuse the existing event.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Avoids two events for one action, which double-counts the funnel.
